_note: Batch 11. Six posts, 10 cards, first batch authored under the corrected placement rule (card directly below its section heading). 3116 leads it: four ranking headings on a post that had ZERO cards, the largest rank gap on the site. Cut on the read: 3978's two chest-pain candidates again, because cardneed flags them as already tabled in '4 Key Differences'; 2780 and 3796 likewise; 3921's 'What Pediatric-Friendly Emergency Care Looks Like' because it describes the facility rather than a decision the reader makes (same cut as batch 4); 3875's two candidates, cut on the batch-7 read and still valid; 3979's numbered sub-emergencies because that post already carries an overview card covering all eight; 3894's 'Don't Second-Guess Your Heart Health' because it is a call to action, not a decision aid. 3921's card deliberately answers 'is 103 an emergency' rather than repeating the age-and-temperature thresholds card already live on that post.

cards.subject: skeletal traction
cards.heading: What is Skeletal Traction?
title: Where
Skeletal Traction
Is Used
cards.alt: The three bones where skeletal traction is most effective: the distal femur, the proximal tibia and the cervical spine

cards.subject: skeletal traction
cards.heading: Types of Skeletal Traction
title: The Three Types of
Skeletal Traction
cards.alt: The three types of skeletal traction: balanced traction using counterweights and pulleys, femoral traction for mid-thigh fractures, and tibial traction for lower leg injuries

items.label: Femoral traction
items.note: For mid-thigh fractures, through the femur

items.label: Tibial traction
items.note: For lower leg injuries, through the tibia

cards.subject: skeletal traction
cards.heading: Skeletal Traction Procedure
title: The
Skeletal Traction
Procedure
cards.alt: The five stages of the skeletal traction procedure: preparation, pin or wire insertion, weight and pulley application, post-procedure monitoring, and traction maintenance

cards.subject: bone stimulator
cards.heading: How Bone Stimulators Support Skeletal Traction Recovery
title: When a
Bone Stimulator
Helps
cards.alt: Three situations where a bone stimulator helps recovery: slow healing after surgery, a history of smoking diabetes or osteoporosis, and injury to a weight-bearing bone

items.label: Smoking, diabetes or osteoporosis
items.note: A previous history of any of these

items.label: A weight-bearing bone
items.note: Such as the femur or the tibia

cards.subject: fever
cards.heading: Understanding the 103
title: Is a 103°F
Fever
an Emergency?
cards.alt: When a 103 degree fever is manageable at home and when it needs the ER: an older child still drinking and playing whose fever comes down with medicine, against a persistent fever that does not respond or comes with a stiff neck

cards.subject: DKA
cards.heading: Recognizing the Red Flags: DKA Symptoms
title: DKA
Red Flags
cards.alt: Four DKA red flags: fruity smelling breath, unquenchable thirst, frequent urination, and confusion or mental fatigue

cards.subject: DKA
cards.heading: How the ER Stabilizes Blood Sugar
title: How the ER Treats
DKA
cards.alt: The three pillars of DKA treatment in the emergency room: intravenous fluid replacement, electrolyte replacement, and insulin therapy

steps.label: Fluid replacement
steps.note: IV fluids treat dehydration and dilute excess sugar

cards.subject: headache
cards.heading: When to Visit the ER for a Severe Headache
title: Severe
Headache
: When to Go to the ER
cards.alt: Five red flags that a severe headache needs the emergency room: sudden weakness on one side, speech difficulty, vision changes, fever with a stiff neck, and a first severe headache after age 50

items.label: Sudden weakness or numbness
items.note: Face, arm or leg, often one side

items.label: Vision changes
items.note: Sudden blurring or loss of vision

items.label: Fever with a stiff neck
items.note: Too stiff to touch your chest

cards.subject: rash
cards.heading: Signs Your Rash Needs Urgent Care
title: When a Poison Ivy
Rash
Needs Urgent Care
cards.alt: Five signs a poison ivy rash needs urgent care: rash on the face or eyes, difficulty breathing after exposure, rash over more than a quarter of the body, itching that prevents sleep, and blisters oozing fluid or pus

items.label: On the face or eyes
items.note: Do not treat this at home

cards.subject: DVT
cards.heading: Recognizing DVT Symptoms: More Than Just a Cramp
title: DVT
: What to Look For
cards.alt: Four DVT symptoms to look for, usually in one leg only: swelling with the calf or thigh visibly larger, redness or discoloration, warmth to the touch, and tenderness that can feel like a pulled muscle

items.label: Swelling in one leg
items.note: The calf or thigh looks larger

items.label: Tenderness
items.note: It can feel like a pulled muscle
